options.content:
### Where the data comes from

The City of Melbourne publishes what its sensors measure as open data, on [its portal](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/), with no key. This dashboard reads three of its networks, in the city centre and around it:

- **[On-street parking bay sensors](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/on-street-parking-bay-sensors/)**: a sensor in the road surface under each of some 6,300 bays says whether a car is over it. The portal holds each bay's latest state and when it last changed, refreshed every few minutes. The streets come from the [bays' register](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/on-street-parking-bays/) and, failing that, from the [bay's parking zone](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/parking-zones-linked-to-street-segments/).
- **[Pedestrian counting system](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/pedestrian-counting-system-monthly-counts-per-hour/)**: about 100 counters (laser and thermal sensors on poles and awnings) count the people walking past each way, hour by hour, around the clock since 2009. The counts are loaded once a day, so the latest hours are a day or two old.
- **[Microclimate sensors](https://data.melbourne.vic.gov.au/explore/dataset/microclimate-sensors-data/)**: a dozen stations on poles and rooftops measure temperature, humidity, wind, fine particles and noise about every 15 minutes. Only five still report. The portal sometimes stops updating for days (it has held nothing newer than 18 October 2026 since then): the stations then show their last 14 days or the time range's length, ending at the latest reading, and *Stations last reported* says how old it is.

### How to read it

- A bay's state is now; the time range does not change it. A sensor that has not changed in a week is shown grey and left out of the counts: in the city centre a bay is not taken, or free, that long, so the sensor is taken as broken or switched off. A bay with no sensor does not show at all.
- The pedestrian counts are the time range's, up to its last 31 days; the microclimate readings, up to its last 14.
- **Everything is a filter.** Pick a status or a street, brush how long bays have held, or draw an area on the map: the map filters the bays on the GPU and the cards and the streets follow. The *Time Brush* pinned at the foot of the page picks the hours: the map's counters take their mean hour in them and its stations and surface their last reading, and the pedestrian and microclimate cards, charts and tables follow; press play to slide it. Drag a box on *When the city walks* to keep some hours of the day and days of the week. The filters are [Mosaic](https://idl.uw.edu/mosaic/) selections, answered in your browser.
- Noise is in decibels (dB): 55 dB is a quiet street, 70 dB a busy one with traffic.

### How it works

Grafana's DuckDB reads the three datasets through the stack's gateway, which keeps each a while (the bays and the microclimate two minutes, the counts an hour), so the portal is asked once whoever is looking. DuckDB running in your browser (the Chaski data source) then answers every panel and every click. The map is the Kepler Geospatial Maps Plus panel, with its Sparkline layer; the linked charts and the filters are Chaski's Mosaic and filters panels. The dashboard reloads every five minutes.

spec.description: Every parking filter, each counted under the others: pick a status or a street, brush how long the bays have held their state, or draw an area on the map. A × clears one, Clear all clears them all.

spec.rawSql:
-- People an hour on the bars (under the hour and weekday box of When the city
-- walks, read from its variables: a macro over pedFilters would re-run this on
-- every move of the window it writes) and every hour in grey behind; the median
-- temperature of the stations as a line. The domain is the data, not the time
-- range: the microclimate portal can lag days behind the counters.
WITH p AS (
  SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 HOUR, time::TIMESTAMP) AS time, sum(people)::DOUBLE AS every,
         (sum(people) FILTER (WHERE hour BETWEEN coalesce(try_cast($pedHourLo AS DOUBLE), -1) AND coalesce(try_cast($pedHourHi AS DOUBLE), 99)
                                AND dow BETWEEN coalesce(try_cast($pedDowLo AS DOUBLE), 0) AND coalesce(try_cast($pedDowHi AS DOUBLE), 9)))::DOUBLE AS kept
  FROM $peds GROUP BY 1
),
c AS (
  SELECT time_bucket(INTERVAL 1 HOUR, time::TIMESTAMP) AS time, median(temperature) AS temp
  FROM $climate GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT coalesce(p.time, c.time) AS time, p.every AS "Every hour", coalesce(p.kept, 0) AS "People an hour", c.temp AS "Temperature"
FROM p FULL JOIN c ON p.time = c.time
ORDER BY 1

The map counters take their mean hour in it, the stations and the surface their last reading in it.

spec.rawSql:
WITH sel AS (SELECT * FROM $peds WHERE $__crossfilter($pedFilters))
SELECT name AS "Counter",
       sum(people)::BIGINT AS "People",
       round(avg(people))::BIGINT AS "Mean hour",
       max(people) AS "Busiest hour",
       arg_max(time, people) AS "When"
FROM sel

WITH last AS (WITH days AS (SELECT day, count(DISTINCT hour) AS hours FROM $peds GROUP BY day)
SELECT max(day) AS day FROM days WHERE hours = 24)
SELECT sum(people)::BIGINT AS "People" FROM $peds, last WHERE $peds.day = last.day

WITH last AS (WITH days AS (SELECT day, count(DISTINCT hour) AS hours FROM $peds GROUP BY day)
SELECT max(day) AS day FROM days WHERE hours = 24)

spec.rawSql:
-- Every bay, coloured by what its sensor says now. Status, street, how long
-- it has held and a drawn area are filtered in the map, on the GPU, where the
-- clauses of the bayFilters selection land.
SELECT bay, zone, street, segment, status, since, minutes, latitude, longitude FROM $bays

-- The mean hour of each counter under the pedestrian brushes (the hours on
-- the timeline, the hour of day and the day of the week): people is the mean
-- count an hour, total the people counted, hours the hours it counted. No
-- quote marks in these comments: Chaski would read a macro after one as text.
SELECT sensor, any_value(name) AS name, any_value(latitude) AS latitude, any_value(longitude) AS longitude,
       round(avg(people))::BIGINT AS people, sum(people)::BIGINT AS total, count(*) AS hours
FROM $peds
WHERE $__crossfilter($pedFilters)
GROUP BY sensor

-- The readings of the Time Brush window or, with no window or none in it,
-- of the last day of readings, one row each: the Surface takes the last
-- reading of each station, the cards chart them. The colours span these rows
-- only: a week of temperatures (5 to 28 °C) would paint the degree or two
-- between stations at one moment in a single band. The Measure picker gives
-- the column drawn as "value" (Chaski quotes the value of a variable; :raw
-- gives the bare column name). A station that lacks the measure (Royal Park
-- has no noise or particles) drops out.
WITH r AS (SELECT * FROM $climate WHERE ${metric:raw} IS NOT NULL),
win AS (SELECT * FROM r WHERE $t0 <> '' AND $__crossfilter($climateFilters)),
pick AS (
  SELECT * FROM win
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM r WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM win) AND time > (SELECT max(time) FROM r) - INTERVAL 24 HOUR
)
SELECT station, place, time, temperature, humidity, wind, noise, pm25,
       ${metric:raw} AS value,
       printf('%.1f', ${metric:raw})
         || CASE ${metric} WHEN 'temperature' THEN ' °C' WHEN 'humidity' THEN ' %' WHEN 'noise' THEN ' dB'
                           WHEN 'pm25' THEN ' µg/m³' ELSE '' END AS reading,
       latitude, longitude
FROM pick
ORDER BY station, time

The white dots are the microclimate stations, with their latest temperature and street noise. Click a counter to see it below.

spec.description: The microclimate measure the stations and the surface draw.

spec.name: metric
spec.query: Temperature (°C) : temperature,Humidity (%) : humidity,Wind speed : wind,Street noise (dB) : noise,Fine particles PM2.5 (µg/m³) : pm25

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: every parking bay sensor the City of Melbourne runs, and what
-- it says now, through the gateway, which keeps the list two minutes (see
-- gateway/feeds.conf). Each bay's street comes from the bays' register, by
-- kerbside id. The timestamp is when the bay last changed: a bay that has not
-- changed in a week is taken as a sensor gone quiet, not a car parked for it.
WITH sensors AS (
  SELECT kerbsideid, zone_number, status_description, status_timestamp,
         ST_Y(location) AS latitude, ST_X(location) AS longitude
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/on-street-parking-bay-sensors.parquet')
),
streets AS (
  SELECT TRY_CAST(kerbsideid AS BIGINT) AS kerbsideid, any_value(roadsegmentdescription) AS segment
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/on-street-parking-bays.parquet?select=kerbsideid,roadsegmentdescription&where=kerbsideid%20is%20not%20null')
  GROUP BY 1
),
zones AS (
  SELECT parkingzone AS zone_number, any_value(onstreet) AS onstreet,
         any_value(onstreet || ' between ' || streetfrom || ' and ' || streetto) AS zsegment
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/parking-zones-linked-to-street-segments.parquet')
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT s.kerbsideid::VARCHAR                                  AS bay,
       s.zone_number                                         AS zone,
       coalesce(t.segment, z.zsegment, 'Unknown')            AS segment,
       coalesce(nullif(regexp_extract(t.segment, '^(.*?) between ', 1), ''), t.segment, z.onstreet, 'Unknown') AS street,
       CASE WHEN s.status_timestamp < now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY THEN 'Silent for a week'
            WHEN s.status_description = 'Present'           THEN 'Occupied'
            ELSE 'Free' END                                  AS status,
       s.status_timestamp                                    AS since,
       date_diff('minute', s.status_timestamp, now())        AS minutes,
       s.latitude, s.longitude
FROM sensors AS s
LEFT JOIN streets AS t USING (kerbsideid)
LEFT JOIN zones AS z USING (zone_number)

spec.label: Pedestrian counts (one row per counter and hour)
spec.name: peds

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: every pedestrian counter's hourly count over the time range,
-- through the gateway (see gateway/feeds.conf). The city loads the counts
-- once a day, so the latest hours are a day or two old. Whole days in
-- Melbourne, at most the last 31, so one URL stands for a day and the cache
-- can answer it. (A table function takes no subquery, so the dates are
-- written out in place.) A row's time is the start of its hour; day and hour
-- are Melbourne's (dow: 1 Monday to 7 Sunday). dir_1 and dir_2 are the two ways past the counter, named by
-- way_1 and way_2.
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT * FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/pedestrian-counting-system-monthly-counts-per-hour.parquet?select=location_id,sensing_date,hourday,direction_1,direction_2,pedestriancount&where=sensing_date%3E%3D%22'
                             || strftime(greatest(timezone('Australia/Melbourne', make_timestamptz(CAST(${__from} AS BIGINT) * 1000)), timezone('Australia/Melbourne', make_timestamptz(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) * 1000)) - INTERVAL 31 DAY), '%Y-%m-%d')
                             || '%22%20and%20sensing_date%3C%3D%22' || strftime(timezone('Australia/Melbourne', make_timestamptz(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) * 1000)), '%Y-%m-%d') || '%22')
),
places AS (
  SELECT location_id, sensor_description, direction_1 AS way_1, direction_2 AS way_2, latitude, longitude
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/pedestrian-counting-system-sensor-locations.parquet')
)
SELECT c.location_id::VARCHAR                                                   AS sensor,
       coalesce(p.sensor_description, 'Sensor ' || c.location_id)            AS name,
       timezone('Australia/Melbourne', c.sensing_date + to_hours(c.hourday))  AS time,
       strftime(c.sensing_date, '%Y-%m-%d')                                   AS day,
       c.hourday                                                              AS hour,
       isodow(c.sensing_date)                                                 AS dow,
       c.pedestriancount                                                      AS people,
       c.direction_1 AS dir_1, c.direction_2 AS dir_2, p.way_1, p.way_2,
       p.latitude, p.longitude
FROM counts AS c LEFT JOIN places AS p USING (location_id)
WHERE p.latitude IS NOT NULL

-- Server side: the readings of the city's microclimate stations through the
-- gateway (see gateway/feeds.conf). A station reports every 15 minutes or so;
-- some have gone quiet, and only those reporting show up. The portal has also
-- stopped updating for days at a time (from 18 October 2026, for one), so the
-- window ends at the latest reading it holds when that is before the time
-- range's end: as long as the range, at most 14 days, never empty. The latest
-- reading is asked first (one row, ordered by the portal). Whole hours, so one
-- URL stands for an hour. The Royal Park weather station measures no noise or
-- particles.
SET VARIABLE last_reading = (
  SELECT max(received_at)
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/microclimate-sensors-data.parquet?select=received_at&order_by=received_at%20desc&limit=1'));
SET VARIABLE window_end = date_trunc('hour', least(make_timestamp(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) * 1000),
                                                   coalesce(getvariable('last_reading')::TIMESTAMP, make_timestamp(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) * 1000))))
                          + INTERVAL 1 HOUR;
SET VARIABLE window_start = getvariable('window_end')
                            - to_milliseconds(least(CAST(${__to} AS BIGINT) - CAST(${__from} AS BIGINT), 14 * 86400000))
                            - INTERVAL 1 HOUR;
SELECT device_id                                   AS station,
       sensorlocation                              AS place,
       received_at                                 AS time,
       airtemperature                              AS temperature,
       relativehumidity                            AS humidity,
       averagewindspeed                            AS wind,
       gustwindspeed                               AS gust,
       pm25, pm10, noise,
       ST_Y(latlong) AS latitude, ST_X(latlong) AS longitude
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/melbourne/microclimate-sensors-data.parquet?where=received_at%3E%3D%22'
                  || strftime(getvariable('window_start'), '%Y-%m-%dT%H:00:00Z')
                  || '%22%20and%20received_at%3C%22'
                  || strftime(getvariable('window_end'), '%Y-%m-%dT%H:00:00Z') || '%22')
WHERE latlong IS NOT NULL
